purpose: Bind a current same-account public-vs-private GitHub Actions control test.
verified_inference: The GlacierEQ account can currently obtain and execute a GitHub-hosted ubuntu runner on a public repository. The mega-skills failure is therefore not an account-wide GitHub-hosted-runner outage. The remaining GitHub fault domain is private-repository-specific Actions eligibility, repository Actions settings, or private-repository billing/usage policy.
provider_route_failures: Repository Actions administration endpoint is blocked by the connected GitHub endpoint allowlist despite repository admin permission.
No current September billing/payment/quota notification was located in connected Gmail; only the August 31 90% and 100% included-minutes notices were found.
Buildkite #522 is visible only as a failed commit status target; exact job/command output is not exposed by the connected GitHub status surface.
Direct Buildkite web/API access is unavailable in this invocation, no Buildkite plugin is installed, and the Operator host is offline.

objective_state_delta.before: The incident was bounded to provider-side runner allocation, but account-wide versus private-repository-specific eligibility remained unresolved.
objective_state_delta.after: A same-account public repository has current successful hosted-runner execution while the private mega-skills repository simultaneously returns runner_id=0 and no steps. Account-wide hosted-runner outage is falsified; investigation is narrowed to private-repository eligibility/settings/billing.

next_frontier: Use an admin-capable GitHub billing/settings surface to inspect and repair mega-skills private-repository Actions eligibility; use an authenticated Buildkite or restored Operator-host route to recover build 522's exact failing command.
